questions.q: What is the highest ledger protocol version this stellar-core build supports, and where is that number actually set?
questions.hardReason: The obvious name, Config::CURRENT_LEDGER_PROTOCOL_VERSION in Config.cpp, is only an alias; the literal number lives in a util header.

evidence.note: MAX_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION is a constexpr set to 30, with one added when built with ENABLE_NEXT_PROTOCOL_VERSION_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION (lines 14 to 17).
Config::CURRENT_LEDGER_PROTOCOL_VERSION is defined as equal to MAX_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION; it names the concept but holds no number.
Declares the static CURRENT_LEDGER_PROTOCOL_VERSION member without a value.

questions.q: Where is the stellar-core `calculate-asset-supply` command line subcommand implemented?
questions.pathsNote: Both count as full answers: CommandLine.cpp holds the subcommand's handler and its registration in the command table; ApplicationUtils.cpp holds the body that walks the bucket lists and sums the supply. A developer asking 'where is it implemented' is served by either.

evidence.note: runCalculateAssetSupply parses --code and --issuer into an Asset and delegates to calculateAssetSupply.
The command table registers the name calculate-asset-supply with its help text and runCalculateAssetSupply.
calculateAssetSupply builds an offline Application, loads the last closed ledger, and sums balances, starting from the fee pool for the native asset.
Describes what calculate-asset-supply does; documentation only.

questions.q: How does a Soroban contract refer to host objects through a Val, and can a guest forge or allocate object handles itself? Which doc section explains it?

evidence.note: Explains that handles sit in the high 32 bits of a Val, are allocated only by the host, and are translated through per-guest tables so guests cannot reach objects not passed to them.

questions.q: When I run the released stellar-rpc binary, what are the default and maximum page sizes for getLedgers, and where are they set?
questions.hardReason: There are two config layers. rpcv2/config/config.go sets getLedgers to 20 max and 5 default, but rpcv2 is not released: the release build refuses --enable-rpcv2, and rpcv1 is the default mode. The released values (200 and 50) are in the rpcv1 options.

evidence.note: Option max-ledgers-limit defaults to 200, and default-ledgers-limit (line 380) defaults to 50 with a check that the default cannot exceed the max.
The rpcv2-only constants set getLedgers max 20 and default 5; these apply only with --enable-rpcv2, which needs a RPCV2=true build.
Context: ModeRPCv1 is documented as the default mode. Makefile lines 68 to 70 say rpcv2 is not released yet.

questions.q: If I run the stellar/quickstart image without any --enable flag, which services start? Is Stellar Lab among them?
questions.hardReason: The README Service Options section says the default is all services and shows core,horizon,rpc,lab. The start script's actual default leaves out lab.

evidence.note: ENABLE defaults to core,horizon,rpc when unset; process_args (lines 222 to 240) turns each listed name into an ENABLE_* flag, so lab stays off.
The GitHub Action's enable input also defaults to core,horizon,rpc, but that is the Action's own input, not the image's.
Claims enabling all services is the default and shows core,horizon,rpc,lab, which does not match start.
